title: Can You Mix Baking Soda and Vinegar for Cleaning?

seo.title: Can You Mix Baking Soda and Vinegar for Cleaning?
seo.meta_description: You can mix baking soda and vinegar, but the fizz does not mean the mixture keeps the full cleaning power of both products.
seo.search_intent: Understand “can you mix baking soda and vinegar for cleaning” and turn the explanation into a practical, clear, and safe household decision.

excerpt: You can mix baking soda and vinegar, but the fizz does not mean the mixture keeps the full cleaning power of both products. The acid and base largely neutralize each other, so they are often more useful separately.
content_html:
You can mix baking soda and vinegar, but the fizz does not mean the mixture keeps the full cleaning power of both products. The acid and base largely neutralize each other, so they are often more useful separately.

The fizz is an acid-base reaction

Baking soda releases carbon dioxide when it reacts with acetic acid in vinegar. The bubbling can help disturb loose debris, but it does not create a miracle cleaner.

Use vinegar for compatible mineral deposits

Vinegar can help dissolve mineral scale on acid-safe surfaces. Do not use it on natural stone or finishes whose manufacturer warns against acids.

Use baking soda when you need mild abrasion

A damp paste can help on some durable surfaces, but it can still scratch glossy or delicate finishes. Test first.

Do not store the mixture in a sealed container

The reaction produces gas. Mixing the ingredients and sealing them in a bottle can build pressure; once the fizzing stops, most of the reaction has already happened.
